title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator on mobile takes notes of in-person conversations with speaker attribution
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned mobile speaker attribution change from existing Facilitator capabilities and the Teams Rooms preview. Its availability path, PowerShell command and general licensing statements are documented, and it identifies the conflicting admin guidance without presenting mobile-specific unknowns as established behaviour.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents > agent > Edit availability reaches the built-in agent availability control.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and go to Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents. ... To change who can use an agent, select one or more agents and choose Edit availability.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <Facilitator-app-id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone uses documented parameters to set app availability to Everyone.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone ... Updates the availability value for Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b) to Everyone.

claims.claim: Built-in agent availability controls who can use Facilitator across the tenant, with everyone, specific users or groups, and no one as choices.
claims.quote: Built-in Teams agents like Channel Agent, Facilitator ... are managed from the Built-In Teams agents page ... You can make an agent available to everyone, to specific users or groups, or to no one.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly state that the app-centric availability command also covers the dedicated Built-in Teams agents route.
claims.quote: Searched: Built-in Teams agents PowerShell Facilitator; Facilitator mobile note taking PowerShell policy control Update-M365TeamsApp. Read manage-apps, app-centric-management and Update-M365TeamsApp; none explicitly connects the cmdlet to the dedicated built-in agent page.

claims.where: controls[1]; summary; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No tenant switch specifically for mobile capture or mobile speaker attribution is documented on either the admin UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Facilitator mobile note taking PowerShell policy control Update-M365TeamsApp; Facilitator mobile speaker attribution license default control. Read facilitator-teams, manage-apps, app-centric-management and Update-M365TeamsApp; only general availability and meeting controls were documented.

claims.claim: The setup page gives Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block, whereas the management overview places Facilitator under Built-in Teams agents.
claims.quote: In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Facilitator from the app list. ... In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.claim: The Facilitator setup page points administrators to app-centric management for availability.
claims.quote: You can also use app centric management to allow and block, create policies, and assign users.

claims.claim: Loop experiences in Teams control AI-generated meeting notes through the IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled PowerShell setting.
claims.quote: Loop experiences in Teams control AI-generated notes for meetings, which are enabled by default. You can manage this control using the IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled setting in PowerShell.

claims.claim: The documented IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled control applies tenant-wide.
claims.quote: This setting applies to your entire tenant and can't be configured at the user level.

claims.claim: The documented meeting Loop control is not explicitly confirmed for phone-started conversations.
claims.quote: Searched: Facilitator mobile capture default admin action Loop prerequisites; Facilitator mobile note taking PowerShell policy control Update-M365TeamsApp. Read facilitator-teams; its IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled passage specifies notes for meetings, without addressing ad hoc phone capture.

claims.claim: The Teams Rooms page limits identification and attribution to participants who add their names at the beginning of the session.
claims.quote: Currently, only participants who add their names at the beginning of the meeting session will be identified and attributed, provided that they have enrolled their profiles.

claims.claim: Those Teams Rooms participants must also have enrolled their profiles to be attributed.
claims.quote: Currently, only participants who add their names at the beginning of the meeting session will be identified and attributed, provided that they have enrolled their profiles.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the Teams Rooms speaker identification prerequisites also apply to phones.
claims.quote: Searched: Facilitator mobile speaker attribution license default control; Facilitator Teams mobile speaker attribution storage notes license default administrator control PowerShell.
